messages:
melissa.gray: Heads up — since ~09:10 UTC we've been seeing intermittent token-stream stalls for hosted inference in us-west-2. p99 token latency spikes from ~120ms to >2s and a bunch of gRPC deadline errors in the logs. Noticed this coincides with a spike in retransmits and out-of-order packets on the gpu-service pod network paths.
ben_irwin: Ugh. Any obvious MTU changes/deploys around that time? Could be fragmentation or offload interaction (GSO/TSO) causing reordering under load.
carlos.runtime: I saw a few `deadline exceeded` traces from the streaming proxy: clients get a bunch of `STATUS: UNAVAILABLE` and then a long pause before tokens resume. Runtime sees lots of inflight stalled requests and KV cache churn. Not sure if retries are compounding it.
anya.sre: Can we get a quick packet capture on a few affected nodes? tcpdump capturing seq/order should show reordering pattern. Also want to check RDMA counters if those hosts use RoCE — `ibv_devinfo` and `/sys/class/net/<iface>/statistics`.
melissa.gray: Captured a short tcpdump on worker-azb-12. Attaching snippet:
```
12:34:56.789 IP a.b.c.d.45678 > x.y.z.w.443: Flags [.], seq 12345:12567, ack 9876, win 65535, length 222
12:34:56.789 IP a.b.c.d.45678 > x.y.z.w.443: Flags [.], seq 12567:12889, ack 9876, win 65535, length 322
12:34:56.790 IP a.b.c.d.45678 > x.y.z.w.443: Flags [.], seq 12000:12345, ack 9876, win 65535, length 345  <-- late arrival
```
melissa.gray: That out-of-order triple is classic NIC/GSO reorder under heavy burst. Same pattern across 4 different hosts in the rack.
ben_irwin: If it's GSO/GRO/TSO, try disabling on one host as a quick repro: `ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off` and see streaming behavior. Also `ethtool -S eth0` for driver counters.
anya.sre: I ran `ethtool -S` on two affected nodes — aggregated tx_packets look normal but `rx_nohandler` and `rx_missed_errors` spiked. Also checked NIC firmware versions: some are on 23.2.x and others on 22.8.x — might be a regression in the newer firmware with VXLAN + offloads.
carlos.runtime: On runtime side I toggled per-connection inflight tokens to 8 from 32 for a canary on one pool; it reduced stall impact (fewer simultaneous in-flight chunks to reorder), but throughput dropped ~18% for that pool.
infra-bot: [alert] network.reordering.usw2.gpu-pool — 2026-03-18T09:17:21Z — autoscale: suspended for impacted pool(s) while investigating.
ben_irwin: For hosts using RoCE, check PFC/ECN settings — head-of-line and priority flow controls can interact badly. If it's pure TCP over VXLAN, kernel offload bug is more likely. Also try toggling `net.core.rps_sock_flow_entries` and RFS to see if steering helps.
melissa.gray: Good call. I ran a quick test disabling GSO/GRO on one ToR-facing host + pinned a canary client to the same ToR. Token stalls went away for that canary. Re-enabling showed stalls reappear. So likely driver/firmware + offload interaction.
anya.sre: Plan: (1) roll a targeted kernel/driver + NIC firmware update to the affected rack tomorrow morning (2) apply a short-term workaround globally: set `GSO/GRO` off on the worker NICs in the GPU pools if firmware update not feasible quickly (3) runtime: keep lower inflight per-conn and increase RPC deadline to 6s as safety net for streaming.
carlos.runtime: I'll open a runtime ticket to adjust default inflight and graceful retry behavior; we should also add better instrumentation to correlate reorder events with token stall traces.
ben_irwin: Also add a qdisc qlen check — `tc -s qdisc show dev eth0` — we've seen large backlog spikes on a few nodes which increase coalescing windows and worsen reordering.
melissa.gray: Scheduling a maintenance window 09:00 PT tomorrow to flash NIC firmware + driver on the affected AZb rack, canary first. Avoid mass reboot of GPU hosts in production; will migrate workloads off each host before update.
deploy-bot: Deployment window created: https://deploys.internal/ops/INC-5487 — owners: @melissa.gray @ben_irwin. Canary start: 2026-03-19T16:00Z.
anya.sre: For tracking, I created an infra-kernel-issue: INC-5487 and linked kernel logs + the tcpdump samples. Also noted impacted GPU capacity: estimated ~8% of pooled capacity effectively degraded due to stalls; we'll alert capacity planning to avoid overcommit for next 48h.
melissa.gray: Thanks — good triage. Action items: firmware+driver canary, global GSO/GRO off if canary confirms, runtime inflight/deadline tweak, and follow-up postmortem with perf numbers. I'll post updates in #incidents once canary completes.
